text:
CHAIN:
L1: Replace per-channel RMSNorm gains with one scalar per norm -> fewer non-embedding params, and per-channel scaling freedom is removed | quantity: params_nonembed | baseline: 21.24M | expect: down 9.5k–12.7k (it depends on which norms are included: 25 scalars give −9,575 and 61 scalars give −12,611; neither matches the stated −9,560) | breaks if: --build-only reports a delta outside that band (the wrong set of norms was converted).
L2: A q-side scalar initialized so that q·k starts at 1.4x -> sharper early attention | quantity: attention entropy by layer and max attention logit | baseline: entropy 0.667–0.957; max logit 7.8–22.75 | expect: at step 100, mid and late entropy down 0.01–0.08 and layer 0 roughly unchanged; max logit up by less than 3 | breaks if: entropy at layers 3–11 changes by less than ±0.01. That would mean the unnormalized rotary part (qr/kr), not the content temperature, sets attention sharpness.
L3: The final norm loses its per-channel gain, so the tied head reads exactly the input-embedding geometry. This removes the only per-channel decoupling between the input and output embeddings | quantity: matched-step training loss, split by the token-frequency buckets | baseline: rank 0–100: 3.163; rank 10000+: 11.613 | expect: frequent bucket within ±0.02 at step 100; rare bucket within ±0.05 | breaks if: the rare-token bucket is worse by more than 0.05 at step 100 on paired seeds.
L4: Scalars are exempt from decay (or reach a gradient/decay equilibrium) -> the norm output scale stops drifting downward | quantity: trajectory of each scalar, compared with the mean and coefficient of variation (CV) of each baseline gain vector at the end of the run | baseline: unmeasured | expect: baseline n1/n2 gain CV < 0.15 and the scalars stay within 0.7–1.5 | breaks if: the baseline gain vectors end with CV > 0.25 or with channels near 0. That would mean the gains were doing feature selection, not setting a temperature.
L5: Fewer AdamW-driven per-channel parameters -> smaller spread in update size | quantity: ||dw||/||w|| median and max | baseline: 0.02009 / 0.03265 (x2 spread) | expect: max and spread unchanged within ±10% | breaks if: the spread falls by more than 15%. That would be evidence the gains contributed to it. A null result here refutes the stated TARGET, not the idea.
L6: All of the above -> exam loss | quantity: exam val_loss (3+ seeds) and paired loss_curve | baseline: step-100 train loss 6.1789; pooled exam mean unmeasured here | expect: mean of steps 36–45 within ±0.03; step 100 within −0.02 to +0.01; final within −0.01 to +0.01 | breaks if: the final val is worse by more than 0.005 on the pooled seeds (the idea hurts), or if the 0.005 improvement is not reached at p<0.01 (the idea does nothing, which is the most likely failure).
WEAKEST: L4

QUESTIONS:
Q1: Which norms become scalar: only n1/n2/final (which is where the 9,600 count comes from), or also latent_norm, q_norm and k_norm? | decides: 25 scalars (−9,575) vs 61 scalars (−12,611)
A1: 12×(384+384)+384 = 9,600, so the stated count covers only the stream read-out norms and the final norm. The "attention temperature at 1.4x" can only live in q_norm/k_norm, because n1's output is renormalized before the content logits. So for the mechanism to exist, the q/k norms must be converted. The faithful build is all 37 norms converted, giving 61 scalars. The stated −9,560 matches neither option and should be corrected to −12,611.

Q2: What does n1's scalar actually control in this script? | decides: keep a scalar on n1 vs make n1 purely no-affine
A2: `qc` is renormalized by q_norm, and k/v pass through compress→latent_norm, which removes n1's scale. n1's scalar therefore reaches only `qr` (via wq) and `kr` (via `rotary`), so the rotary-part logits scale as s². It is a rotary temperature. Keep it, initialized at 1.0, and name it as such.

Q3: Should the temperature be one learned scalar on q_norm, a scalar on each of q_norm and k_norm, or a fixed `scale=` passed to SDPA? | decides: one learned scalar per layer, init 1.4, with k_norm no-affine vs two scalars, each init √1.4
A3: The SDPA default scale is 1/√96, since q is 64+32 wide. With unit gains the maximum content logit is therefore 64/√96 ≈ 6.5, and 1.4x makes it about 9.1. Two scalars multiply into one product and add only redundant gradient scaling. One scalar on q_norm, initialized at 1.4, is the clean build. Caveat: the measured max logits already reach 22.75, which is far above 6.5. The rotary part (or gain growth) likely dominates, so the 1.4x may barely matter (see L2).

Q4: Should the scalars be weight-decayed? | decides: leave them in the existing AdamW group (wd 0.1) vs put them in a new no-decay AdamW group
A4: `build_optimizers` sends every non-2-D parameter, including 0-D ones, to AdamW with wd 0.1. The decoupled decay factor over 1,525 steps at lr 3e-3, with a mean LR multiplier of about 0.84, is exp(−0.38) ≈ 0.68 in the absence of gradient. The stated mechanism ("no longer fighting decay") only holds if the scalars are exempt, so add a no-decay group.

Q5: Is the final-norm gain redundant? | decides: scalar final norm (faithful) vs keep the 384-wide final gain as an exception
A5: The n1, n2 and latent gains can be absorbed into the next linear layer (a diagonal input scaling), so they are redundant in parameterization. The final gain cannot be absorbed, because the head is tied to `tok`. q/k gains cannot be absorbed either, because they come after the normalization. modded-nanogpt's no-gain evidence comes from an untied head, so it does not cover this case. Whether the gain matters here is unknown. Build it faithfully as a scalar and watch the rare-token bucket (L3).

Q6: How should the scalar be applied? | decides: `F.rms_norm(x, (d,), s.expand(d), eps)` vs `F.rms_norm(x, (d,), None, eps) * s`
A6: The two are mathematically identical. The expand form keeps a single fused kernel; a stride-0 weight may be copied internally, but that is only d floats. The multiply form adds one elementwise pass, about 3 MB of bf16 per call at micro_batch 4, and saves one activation for backward. Use the expand form. The change in VRAM and step time is well inside C4 either way.

Q7: Can a 45-step check with a 0.03 threshold separate signal from noise? | decides: compare loss at step 45 alone vs compare the mean of loss_curve[35:45] on paired seeds
A7: At equal seed, the data order is identical, because `Shards` is seeded only by `cfg.seed`. The linear-layer init is also identical, provided the scalars are created with `torch.full` or `torch.tensor` (no RNG draws) and module creation order is unchanged. Paired differences are therefore clean. A single-step loss over 32k tokens still carries a few hundredths of noise, so compare the 10-step mean.

Q8: Is the proposed TEST ("baseline gains within 10% of uniform → removal safe") informative? | decides: run a separate 500-step probe vs read the gains from an existing full-budget baseline `model.pt`
A8: Uniform shrinkage from decay is not idleness. A small CV does not prove the gains are unused; it only shows a scalar could replace them. The baseline `model.pt` already contains every gain vector at the full budget, so read the per-vector mean and CV there at no cost. The mean of the baseline's q_norm·k_norm product is the empirically learned temperature, and it should set the init instead of 1.4.

Q9: Can removing the gains lower the update-norm spread (the TARGET)? | decides: keep update spread as the success metric vs replace it with entropy plus paired loss
A9: Under Adam, the gains move at roughly lr, about 3e-3, relative to a value of about 1, which is below the 0.020 median. They cannot be the 0.0327 maximum. The spread comes from Muon matrices, where the shape scale reaches √6 for `expand` (768×128). Replace the target.

KNOWN:
- The norms and their widths per block are n1 384, n2 384, latent_norm 128, q_norm 64, k_norm 64, plus a final norm of 384. That totals 12,672 gain parameters. [script]
- n1's scale reaches only qr/kr (the rotary logits). latent_norm's scale reaches only v, because k is renormalized by k_norm. n2's scale enters both silu(gate) and up, so the MLP output scales roughly as s². [script]
- SDPA uses its default scale of 1/√96 because q/k are 64 content + 32 rotary dims wide. [script]
- `read_logits` and `write_logits` are 2-D (2×4) and currently go to Muon; `mix_logits` is 3-D and goes to AdamW. Do not change this in the same build, because it would confound the comparison. [script]
- 0-D parameters fall into the AdamW "other" group automatically. A new no-decay group requires editing `build_optimizers`. [script]
- Full run length: 50e6/32768 = 1,525 steps; warmup 30 steps; cooldown starts at step 1,067. [script]
- The scalars must not draw from torch RNG, or the paired-seed init alignment is lost. [script]
- Layer-0 attention gradient is 0.24, against about 0.02–0.03 elsewhere (z 7.03, 3 seeds). The likely cause is the tiny raw-embedding stream (std 0.02), and gains do not address it. [measured]
- Residual RMS grows from 1.403 to 10.893 across depth. Pre-norm read-outs hide this, so the scalars do not see it. [measured]
- The max attention logit reaches 22.75 at layer 8 despite QK-norm. Content logits are capped near 6.5 at unit gain, so rotary logits or gain growth supply the rest. [measured+script]
- modded-nanogpt applies rms_norm without learned weights. https://github.com/kellerjordan/modded-nanogpt [web]
- modded-nanogpt's attention scale is about 1.36x of 1/√d_head (0.12 vs 1/√128). This is recalled from the repo and not re-checked. [belief]
- Gemma's RMSNorm uses a (1+w) gain, so weight decay pulls it toward identity. https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/gemma/modeling_gemma.py [web]

ASSUMES:
- The per-channel gains act as temperatures and not as feature selectors. In particular, the final norm under a tied head is not doing feature selection.
- Muon can learn per-input-channel scaling inside `wq`, `compress`, `rotary`, `w_gate` and `w_up` as cheaply as a diagonal gain trained with Adam.
- Attention sharpness is limited by the content-part temperature and not by the unnormalized rotary part.
- A temperature of 1.4x is near-optimal at d_head 64 + 32 rotary dims, at 21M parameters and 1,525 steps.
- Weight decay on the gains is harmful enough to matter within 1,525 steps.
- The scaled branch init (std 0.02/√24 on wo/w_down) stays and does not interact with the scalars.

NEW IDEAS:
SLOT: drop
IDEA: Zero-parameter norms with fixed constant temperatures
MECHANISM: Drop the assumption that temperatures must be learned. Every norm becomes no-affine, SDPA gets a fixed `scale=1.4/sqrt(96)`, and the head logits get a fixed multiplier taken from the baseline's learned final-gain mean. This removes all 12,672 parameters with no new ones.
PREDICTION: Loss at step 100 is within 0.02 of baseline; the final loss is within ±0.01; the parameter count drops by 12,672.
TEST: Read the baseline `model.pt` gain means to set the constants, then run a 45-step paired smoke.

SLOT: strengthen
IDEA: Log-parameterized, no-decay scalar temperatures with a boosted LR
MECHANISM: Each scalar becomes s = exp(θ) with θ initialized at log(init), placed in an AdamW group with wd 0 and 5x lr_adam. This makes the steps multiplicative and keeps the temperature free of decay.
PREDICTION: The scalars settle by step 200, with a band of about 0.6–2.0. Mid-layer attention entropy at step 100 is below the plain-scalar variant by at least 0.01.
TEST: A 100-step paired run, logging the θ trajectories and per-layer entropy.

SLOT: specialise
IDEA: Collapse gains to their mean at cooldown start
MECHANISM: Per-channel gains train normally until step 1,067. At that point each vector is replaced by its mean and frozen to a trainable scalar, so the 30% cooldown phase runs without per-channel gain noise.
PREDICTION: The loss jump at the collapse step is under 0.01 if the gains were near-uniform; final loss is within ±0.01 of baseline.
TEST: Collapse at step 100 of a 150-step run and measure the immediate loss jump.

SLOT: port
IDEA: Embedding output multiplier √d (unit-RMS stream entry)
MECHANISM: Multiply `tok(idx)` by √384 ≈ 19.6 before expanding to 4 streams, so the stream starts at RMS about 0.4 instead of 0.02. This targets the 10x layer-0 gradient anomaly through the norm Jacobian (∝ 1/RMS).
PREDICTION: The layer-0 attention gradient falls from about 0.24 toward 0.05–0.10 at step 100; loss at step 100 is within −0.03 to +0.01.
TEST: A 100-step paired run, reading per-layer gradient norms.

SLOT: combine
IDEA: Scalar norms + LayerNorm Scaling, without scaled branch init
MECHANISM: Each n1/n2 scalar is initialized at 1/√(l+1) and trained without decay. The 1/√(2·n_layer) branch init is removed, following LNS v3's finding that the two interact badly. The doubly stochastic mixing is left to carry the residual.
PREDICTION: Residual RMS growth falls from x7.8 to below x5; late-layer entropy rises by 0.02–0.05; final loss changes by −0.015 to +0.01.
TEST: A 100-step paired run, reading per-layer output RMS and loss.

SLOT: other
IDEA: Normalize the rotary logits too (RoPE-part QK-norm with its own scalar)
MECHANISM: Apply a no-affine RMSNorm to qr and kr before RoPE, with one scalar per layer. Both parts of the logit then have explicit temperatures, and the unbounded rotary logit that likely drives the max logit of 22.75 is capped.
PREDICTION: Max attention logit stays below 15 in every layer; loss at step 100 is within ±0.02.
TEST: A 100-step paired run, reading max logits and entropy.
